title: Install and recover Milieu program releases
summary: Install, inspect, or recover Milieu programs and their provider selector. Deployment runs the product-owned file and setup recipe.
use_when: Milieu programs should be installed, inspected, or recovered.
do_not_use_when: Collection or downstream application work should be started.
The requested result is provider billing, credential replacement, destructive state reset or a schedule.
outcome: The supplied programs and provider are selected together, or an explicit setup failure.
effects: Retain supplied programs and documentation in release archives and publish regular files at fixed runtime paths under installation locks. Public file selectors use runtime paths; provider directory selectors use the selected retained archive. Preserve other product selectors and separate product data.
authority: Milieu owns its program installation and provider selector. The operator supplies artifacts and authorizes selection.
success: Owned command and provider selectors follow the supplied release. Installation runs no signature audit, executable probe, or operational-readiness gate.
failure_and_recovery: Refuse foreign public selectors or stale expected-current selections. An instruction failure retains completed file and selector changes for explicit recovery. Recovery selects retained program files and leaves product data unchanged.

Older releases requiring stored collector configuration can fail status or diagnosis on newly initialized Milieu 0.6.0 state even if they read schema-two exports. Recovery does not recreate configuration.
privacy: CLI usage records command identity, time and thread ID without arguments, output or outcomes; recording errors preserve product results.
The frontend reads no provider keys or user shell configuration. Product state and exports remain private caller-owned data.
does_not_authorize: A collection run, schedule, provider purchase, credential replacement, state deletion or downstream application workflow.

consumers.statement: The current user may install or recover Milieu programs through a trusted tested candidate, inspect selectors and understand the restricted frontend environment.

preconditions.statement: Supplied program and provider paths, an intended installation home, and authority to change owned selectors. Installation does not require a validation receipt.

inputs.statement: Absolute binary and bundle paths, optional home and expected-current selection, or one retained release path for recovery.

outputs.statement: Recorded release metadata and selected public paths, or an installation error. Inspection reports metadata without checking artifact integrity.

data_semantics.statement: Program selection is installation state. It establishes neither database integrity nor dependency readiness nor domain success.

identity_and_units.statement: Opaque UUID release IDs name retained archives; executable files run at fixed actual paths beneath Milieu/install/runtime. Product releases, provider contract versions, and application state versions remain distinct. Installation does not compare component versions or artifact hashes.

completeness_and_freshness.statement: Inspection reads current selectors and recorded installation metadata. It does not audit retained content or probe a live dependency.

access.statement: The installed frontend passes HOME, fixed system PATH, optional MILIEU_STATE_DIR, CODEX_THREAD_ID, CHANCERY_USAGE_DB, CHANCERY_USAGE_DISABLED and CHANCERY_USAGE_INTERNAL. It preserves arguments and stdin. It does not source ~/.zshrc or extract provider keys.

lifecycle_and_consistency.statement: Product and catalog locks serialize publication. Regular runtime files are replaced atomically at fixed actual paths; the complete tree is not one atomic update. Expected-current guards detect changed selection. An instruction failure retains completed file and selector changes for explicit recovery. Recovery reads retained metadata without integrity validation and preserves separate product state.

operational_limits.statement: Installation copies files and performs product-owned setup without running executable probes or native-signature audits. It runs no installer verify command, database integrity check, provider validation, or readiness probe. Explicit ordinary diagnostic commands keep their existing behavior.

Deploy accepts one bounded schema-two recipe request on stdin. The product command owns its setup; the shared executor uses process exit status only. Deployment runs no application execution probe, native-signature audit, maintenance hold, drain, or automatic rollback.

Milieu performs no collection. Deployment setup initializes missing schema-two state and rejects unsupported schemas. Optional state_dir is an absolute path; selection uses it, then nonempty inherited MILIEU_STATE_DIR, then ~/.local/share/milieu in the selected home. config_file and collector configuration are removed.

compatibility_and_evolution.statement: Installation contract 4 removes shell credential loading and deployment config_file. Retained release layout and supported installation-metadata readers remain. Program recovery does not restore product data or check program/state compatibility. Select a program that accepts the retained schema.

New state has no collector configuration. Existing metadata can retain old configuration values inertly; Milieu does not read or replace them. Older releases requiring those values can fail status or diagnosis on new state even if they support schema-two exports. Program recovery recreates no configuration.

reliances.statement: Program recovery selects retained files without a state compatibility check and does not restore Milieu data. Setup initializes only supported schema-two state.
